reporting_environment_text: Operators and authorities do not publish event-level outage reports. Events come from media and company statements, so most smaller disruptions will not appear.
reporting_note: Event-level outage reports are not published by operators or regulators. Accident reporting centres on casualties and accountability, not output, and much of it is in Chinese only.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: 31 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities, plus Hong Kong and Macau as special administrative regions, and the Paracel Islands as drawn by Natural Earth. Boundaries show the line of actual control (Natural Earth's default edition), which is an analytic choice, not a statement about sovereignty. Taiwan is not part of this system. The Spratly Islands, which Natural Earth files as a separate disputed unit, are not drawn in this system and no record is placed there; the Paracels are drawn for reference and also take no record.

Paracel Islands: administered by China, claimed by Vietnam and Taiwan. Drawn; never assigned an event.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

release_rule.text: Facility-specific restart, recovery or operating status for a record in a campaign is published only once the campaign is recorded as ended and 30 days have passed. While it is active the event itself is published; its facility status is not.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-10-30 by the China source-audit lane. CONTEXT ONLY, never a scoring input. NBS 2025 figures are preliminary (Communique note 1) and whole-economy scope; NBS monthly releases cover only industrial enterprises above designated size and differ in level (2025 electricity: 9,715.9 vs 10,575.25 billion kWh) - never mix the two scopes. Mainland China only (31 provincial-level units); excludes Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. See docs/countries/CN_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

source_health.origin_rule: An origin is a wire service the citation names, else the website it sits on. Wikipedia and content aggregators are discovery aids and count as no origin. Republication a record does not name cannot be seen, so this can undercount independence but not overstate it.
source_health.first_party_excludes: Wikipedia, whatever role a record gives it
source_health.note: Describes the citations of the published events in this country. Not opened and not recorded are different: a researcher who did not record whether a source was opened is not evidence that it was not. Nothing here is comparable across countries and nothing here enters a number.

research_gaps: Not yet researched: East China industrial power curbs (Aug 2022), winter gas shortages, power-plant outages, and restoration dates for the Sichuan and Chongqing curbs.

lanes.source_family: National statistics: NBS monthly energy production releases (能源生产情况), read for production effects explicitly attributed to a disruption
registry: NBS Statistical Communiqué and monthly energy releases
lanes.finding: Substantive negative finding: across all 53 releases (data months 2021-12 to 2026-09) the NBS energy production release never attributes a production change to a disruption. No release mentions an accident, flood, typhoon, drought or water inflow, weather, shutdown, power rationing, or maintenance, and no release gives a province-level figure: all figures are national totals for above-scale industry. The only causal wording found is supply-policy language attached to coal growth in six releases (data months 2021-12, 2022-03, 2022-04, 2022-05, 2022-06, 2022-11: for example 增产保供政策持续推进, 煤炭保供稳价政策深入推进, 为做好今冬保暖保供工作), plus a days-adjustment phrase for power generation (扣除天数原因) in data months 2025-03 to 2025-08 and a recurring comparability footnote. From 2022-12 onward the text is purely descriptive. Large swings are reported with no stated cause, for example hydro generation -30.0% in 2022-09, -32.9% in 2023-05 and -22.9% for the first half of 2023.
lanes.limitation: Nothing in the universe is unread, but each page was read through WebFetch, which returns a model's reading of the page rather than the raw text; the model declined to reproduce full bodies, so the per-release result rests on its answer to a fixed question asking for every causal phrase verbatim. The attached Excel data tables were not opened. The October 2026 release is not yet published.

lanes.source_family: National Energy Administration and grid companies (State Grid, China Southern Grid): notices of major outages, orderly power use, emergency responses
registry: State Grid and China Southern Grid notices
lanes.finding: The NEA safety department's own listing is the one fully read source here and it is almost silent on events: of 275 titles in the window, 3 concern an actual outage (Gansu earthquake Dec 2023, two items; Hebei Zhuozhou floods Aug 2023) and 1 names an event (Xinjiang 3 Aug 2024 oscillation) without stating any effect. The monthly 事故通报 and 全国电力安全生产情况 series on that listing stop in 2021 (last: Oct 2021 data, published 2021-11-30); nothing in the window replaces them. The site: operator is ignored by the search tool; allowed_domains works for nea.gov.cn, csg.cn and sgcc.com.cn and returned operator pages.
lanes.limitation: State Grid's site did not respond and NEA's general news listing is script-only, so both are unread; China Southern Grid's company-news archive is reachable (20 items a page, paged as index_N.html, by year) but only 3 pages (60 titles) were sampled, and none of the 15 year queries ran before the shared search limit was hit. No English query is declared in the plan and none was run, so the zh+en requirement is not met.

lanes.source_family: Provincial outage and disruption reporting: provincial energy bureaus and government notices of power rationing or grid emergencies
lanes.finding: Yield was plans, not disruptions. Provincial NEA office pages migrated in 2023 carry 2023 dates in their URLs but describe older events (Henan Jan 2018, Zhejiang summer 2013); the search summary presented the Zhejiang 2013 event as 2023. Any record built from these subdomains needs the on-page date.
lanes.limitation: A declared query set, not a census: each query returned about 10 results and only 5 result pages were opened; provincial energy-bureau notice listings were not enumerated. The 'P 大面积停电 应急响应 政府' query returns emergency plans (预案) for almost every province, often from other provinces, and is a poor instrument for finding events.

lanes.source_family: Major state enterprises (Sinopec, PetroChina, CNOOC, China Shenhua, State Power Investment): HKEX and SSE announcements of facility incidents or production susp
registry: State energy enterprise exchange announcements (Sinopec, PetroChina, CNOOC, China Shenhua, SPIC)
lanes.finding: The generic declared queries return mainly pre-2022 events, planned maintenance and share-trading halts (停牌), which the search engine conflates with 停产.
lanes.limitation: The notice archives themselves were not enumerated: HKEX and SSE listings are interactive or script-only, and of the five company notice pages only PetroChina's was reachable, showing its 20 most recent titles (2026-04-29 to 2026-11-05, all routine governance, none about a suspension) with no visible pagination. Annual-report PDFs were not opened. All 15 declared queries ran in both languages, but they are a keyword probe of an archive lane, not a reading of it.

lanes.source_family: Credible Chinese-language media: Xinhua, People's Daily, Caixin, The Paper
registry: Chinese national media (Xinhua, People's Daily, Caixin, The Paper)
lanes.finding: No new qualifying event. Plain refinery queries return foreign refineries almost exclusively; domain-restricted reruns return Xinhua world-desk copy on foreign refineries plus the three domestic events already in the corpus. Coal queries return a recurring pattern in The Paper: listed-company notices of single-mine halts after one-fatality accidents, stating approved capacity but no lost volume (the one stated loss was about 90,000 t). Gas-pipeline queries return only urban distribution incidents (Yanjiao 2024, Anping 2023) and events outside the window (Shiyan 2021, Qinglong) or outside China; no domestic trunk-pipeline shutdown surfaced. 'examined' is an approximate count of result items across 18 searches.
lanes.limitation: A 15-string query set through a general search engine is not a search of the four outlets' archives: Caixin returned no result in any of the 18 searches and People's Daily only a handful, so lane credit rests almost entirely on The Paper and Xinhua.

lanes.source_family: International corroboration: Reuters, Bloomberg, S&P Global reporting of Chinese energy disruptions
registry: International news agencies and energy press (Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, S&P Global, Argus)
lanes.finding: English wire coverage of Chinese power rationing found no firm load shed after 2023: results for 2024, 2025 and 2026 report record demand and renewable curtailment, not rationing. English refinery-fire coverage for 2022-2026 returned only events already in the corpus plus one commissioning fire and one walled headline. Coal-accident coverage is dense but almost never states a supply cut in tonnes; trade press (Mysteel) states halted capacity, behind a login wall.
lanes.limitation: All 15 declared English queries ran and were dispositioned, but this is a query set, not a census, and the wire syndication sites carrying most Reuters and Bloomberg coal stories (mining.com, miningweekly, engineeringnews) refused access, so those articles were judged from headlines. Seen in result lists and not pursued: 2024 Shanxi safety-inspection output curbs (a regulatory campaign, not a discrete event), two mine accidents of 23 Oct 2024 in Hebei and Shanxi, and a reported 2024 output fall in one Heilongjiang city.

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: One automated visit to each cited page. Blocked means the site refused an automated visitor, not that the page is gone. Redirects to a home page or listing count as gone; redirects to a bot check count as blocked.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year
